mainTopic: How the sheep of עצרת make the two loaves holy: the מחלוקת of רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, its explanations, and its practical results
overview: A ברייתא teaches that the two sheep of עצרת (שבועות) make the two loaves holy only through their שחיטה. If both the שחיטה and the זריקה were לשמן, the bread is holy, and if neither was, it is not. In the mixed case, רבי says the bread is 'holy and not holy,' while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is not holy at all. Both learn their views from the פסוק about the נזיר's ram: רבי reads 'יעשה זבח' to mean the doing is the slaughter, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads 'יעשה' to mean all the actions are needed. אביי explains 'holy and not holy' as incomplete holiness, and רבא explains it as full holiness without permission to eat. They differ on whether the holiness passes onto redemption money. Even according to אביי, רבי differs from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about whether the bread becomes unfit by leaving the courtyard. Finally, רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק asks whether the bread may be eaten in the mixed case. The גמרא places his question within a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue whether זריקה affects loaves that left the courtyard.

steps.title: The sheep of עצרת make the bread holy only through slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the basic rule: the sheep of עצרת make the loaves holy only through שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The sheep of עצרת make the bread holy only by being slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets a basic rule. The bread that comes with the sheep of עצרת becomes holy only when the sheep are slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On עצרת two sheep are brought as שלמים together with two loaves. The ברייתא says the sheep make the loaves holy only through their שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The two sheep brought as שלמים on שבועות
Make holy, give a status of קדושה
The bread, here meaning the two loaves of שבועות
Ritual slaughter of the animal

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The sheep of Atzeret
phrases.notes: עצרת is the name the חכמים use for שבועות.

phrases.english: do not make the bread holy
except through slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the sheep and loaves of עצרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves of עצרת become holy only through the שחיטה of the accompanying sheep.

steps.title: Three cases of slaughtering and sprinkling, and the view of רבי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the rule with three cases, depending on whether the שחיטה and the זריקה were done לשמן. In the mixed case, רבי says the bread is partly holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he slaughtered them for their own sake and sprinkled their blood for their own sake, the bread is holy. If he slaughtered them not for their own sake and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake, the bread is not holy. If he slaughtered them for their own sake and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake, the bread is holy and not holy. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out how the rule works by giving three cases. They depend on whether the slaughter and the sprinkling of the blood were done for the right purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both acts are לשמן the bread is fully holy, and when both are not לשמן it is not holy. The middle case is the interesting one. The slaughter was correct but the זריקה was not, so רבי says the bread is in an in-between state, holy and not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? A word that introduces the details of a rule
For their own sake, meaning done with the intent of this specific קרבן
Not for their own sake, meaning done with the wrong intent
Sprinkled their blood on the מזבח (זריקה)
Holy and not holy, a partial or in-between level of holiness

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the opening rule said שחיטה makes the bread holy, רבי rules 'holy and not holy' when the זריקה was not לשמן. The גמרא later explains this phrase in two ways (steps 12–13): אביי says the holiness is incomplete, while רבא says the bread is fully holy but may not be eaten.

phrases.english: How so?
If he slaughtered them for their own sake,
and sprinkled their blood for their own sake,
the bread becomes holy.
If he slaughtered them not for their own sake,
and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake,
the bread does not become holy.
If he slaughtered them for their own sake,
and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake,
the bread is holy and not holy,
these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? שְׁחָטָן לִשְׁמָן, וְזָרַק דָּמָן לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the general rule of step 1 through specific cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both acts לשמן: the bread is holy. Both not לשמן: not holy. שחיטה לשמן but זריקה not לשמן: according to רבי, it is holy and not holy.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: no holiness without both acts done correctly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees with רבי. He holds the bread is never holy unless both the שחיטה and the זריקה were done לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: It is never holy until he slaughters them for their own sake and sprinkles their blood for their own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא argues with רבי about the mixed case. He says the bread gets no holiness at all unless both steps were done correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, a proper שחיטה already gives the bread some holiness. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון there is no in-between state. Both the שחיטה and the זריקה must be לשמן before the bread becomes holy at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Never, in any case (in this phrase: never holy)
Until, meaning only once a condition is met

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is only about the mixed case: proper שחיטה but improper זריקה. רבי says the bread is 'holy and not holy,' while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is not holy at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
it is never holy
until he slaughters them for their own sake
and sprinkles their blood for their own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי's ruling in the mixed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread becomes holy only if both the שחיטה and the זריקה are done לשמן.

steps.title: What is רבי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי's view that the שחיטה alone already gives the bread some holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי gets his view. This line sets up the next step, where the answer comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gave weight to the שחיטה even when the זריקה was done wrong. The גמרא wants to know what source shows that the שחיטה is the act that matters for the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A question asking for the source or logic behind a view

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי's ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי holds that a proper שחיטה alone already gives the bread holiness, even when the זריקה was not לשמן.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that the slaughter makes the bread holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק about the ram of the נזיר: it is offered as a זבח (slaughter-offering) 'with the basket of מצות,' which shows that the שחיטה makes the bread holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall make the ram a זבח of שלמים to ה׳, with the basket of מצות.' This teaches that the slaughter makes the bread holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's source, a פסוק that links the slaughter of a שלמים directly to its bread. From there it learns that the שחיטה is what makes the bread holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word זבח, which is related to slaughtering, and right next to it mentions the basket of מצות. That link shows the bread is tied to the act of שחיטה. So for רבי, a proper שחיטה already gives the bread holiness even if the זריקה goes wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Ram
A peace-offering sacrifice. The word זבח is related to slaughtering
The basket of מצות that comes with the ram of the נזיר
That is to say, meaning this teaches that

steps.whatToRemember: רבי learns from the פסוק of the נזיר's ram that the שחיטה is what makes the accompanying bread holy. That is why, for him, a proper שחיטה gives the bread at least partial holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the general idea behind רבי's view. The bread is tied to the act of שחיטה, not only to the completion of the קרבן through זריקה.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And he shall make the ram
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:17. This is about the ram the נזיר brings when his נזירות ends.

phrases.english: a peace-offering sacrifice to God,
with the basket of matzot,"
which is to say that slaughter makes holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב ״וְאֶת הָאַיִל יַעֲשֶׂה זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים לַה׳ עַל סַל הַמַּצּוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about the נזיר's ram links the זבח (slaughter) to the basket of מצות, which shows that the שחיטה makes the bread holy.

steps.title: The source for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון learns from the word 'יעשה' that the bread is holy only after every action of the offering is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the source of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון? The word 'He shall do' teaches: not until he does all of its actions.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after giving רבי's source, the גמרא gives the source for the other opinion, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the same פסוק about the נזיר's ram but focuses on the word 'יעשה' ('he shall do'). 'Doing' the offering means finishing all its main actions, including the זריקה. So שחיטה alone is not enough to make the bread holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall do / offer.' The word in the פסוק that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון uses.
All of its actions. Here this means the whole service, including זריקה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, what is his source?
'He shall do': not until he does all of its actions.
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:17. This is the same פסוק about the נזיר's ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 5. That step gave רבי's source, and this one gives the source for the other opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'יעשה' means that all the actions must be done, so both the שחיטה and the זריקה are needed.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי: the פסוק also says 'יעשה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי deals with the word 'יעשה,' which seems to require all the actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי too, isn't it written 'He shall do'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי with the word that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון used. It is setting up רבי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions read the same פסוק. If 'יעשה' means all the actions must be done, how can רבי say that שחיטה alone already makes the bread partly holy?

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written…?' A challenge from a word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi too, isn't 'he shall do' written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the word from step 6 against רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that שחיטה alone gives the bread some holiness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'יעשה' seems to require all the actions, and רבי's view should have to explain it.

steps.title: רבי reads the word order: 'do it by slaughtering'
steps.stepSummary: The order 'יעשה זבח' means 'do it by means of slaughtering,' so 'יעשה' points to the שחיטה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it said 'a sacrifice he shall do,' it would be as you say. But now that it says 'he shall do a sacrifice,' it means: how should he do it? By slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי by looking closely at the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זבח' came first, the meaning would be: slaughter it, and then 'do' more, meaning the זריקה. Because 'יעשה' comes first and 'זבח' follows, 'זבח' explains how the 'doing' happens: by זביחה, slaughtering. So for רבי, both words point to the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered offering. Related to the word for slaughtering.
Slaughtering.
'As you are saying.'

steps.confusionAlert: The answer depends only on word order. 'זבח יעשה' and 'יעשה זבח' use the same two words, but they are read differently.

phrases.english: If it were written 'a sacrifice he shall do,'
it would be as you are saying.
phrases.notes: He means: first slaughter, then 'do' something more, which is the זריקה.

phrases.english: Now that it is written 'he shall do … a sacrifice,'
With what shall he do it? With slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יעשה' seems to mean that all the actions are required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because 'יעשה' comes before 'זבח,' the 'doing' is done through slaughtering.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the פסוק says 'זבח'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון deals with the word 'זבח,' which points to slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, isn't it written 'a sacrifice'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the other side the same way. It is setting up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי used 'זבח' to show that the שחיטה makes the bread holy. So what does רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון do with this word?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
isn't 'a sacrifice' written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 7, this time challenging the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that שחיטה alone does not make the bread holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'זבח' seems to give the שחיטה a role, and his view does not account for it.

steps.title: 'זבח' teaches רבי יוחנן's rule: the bread must exist at the שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון uses 'זבח' for a different rule: the bread must already exist when the animal is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word for רבי יוחנן's teaching, because רבי יוחנן said: everyone agrees that the bread must exist at the time of the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון uses the word 'זבח' to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, 'זבח' does not mean that the שחיטה makes the bread holy. It teaches that the bread must be there when the שחיטה happens. Both opinions agree on this rule. They disagree only about whether שחיטה alone makes the bread holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it' for a different teaching.
Everyone agrees.
At the time of the slaughtering.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי reads 'יעשה זבח' to mean that שחיטה makes the bread holy. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads 'יעשה' to mean all the actions are needed, and uses 'זבח' only to require that the bread exist at the שחיטה.

phrases.english: He needs that word
for the teaching of Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees
that the bread must exist at the time of the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זבח' seems to show that the שחיטה makes the bread holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זבח' teaches only that the bread must exist at the שחיטה, a rule everyone agrees to.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the two opinions share common ground. They argue only about when the bread becomes holy, not about whether the bread must be present.

steps.title: What does 'holy and not holy' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי meant when he said the bread is 'holy and not holy' in the mixed case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'holy and not holy' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: explaining רבי's own words from the ברייתא. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mixed case, the שחיטה was done לשמן but the זריקה was not, and רבי said the bread is 'holy and not holy.' That sounds like a contradiction, so the גמרא asks what it really means.

phrases.english: What does 'holy and not holy' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the source discussion and returns to explain רבי's wording in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי's phrase 'holy and not holy'

steps.title: אביי: holy, but not completely
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the bread becomes holy, but its holiness is not complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is holy, but not completely.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first explanation of רבי's phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the two halves of the phrase describe a partial level of holiness. The bread has some holiness, but not the full holiness that comes when the זריקה is also done לשמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, full.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is holy, but not completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bread's holiness is real but incomplete.

steps.title: רבא: holy, but not permitted to be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the bread is holy, but it does not become permitted to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is holy, but it is not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different explanation of רבי's phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the bread does become holy through the שחיטה. The 'not holy' part means it does not become permitted to be eaten. So אביי sees a lower level of holiness, while רבא sees holiness without permission to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, here meaning permitted to be eaten.

steps.whatToRemember: 'Holy and not holy': אביי says holy but not completely; רבא says holy but not permitted to be eaten.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is holy, but it is not permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 11 that differs from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bread is holy, but it is not permitted to be eaten.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between אביי and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what real-world difference there is between the explanations of אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference comes out of the two explanations of אביי and רבא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אביי and רבא agree the bread may not be eaten in this case. So the גמרא wants to know where their two explanations actually lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for a practical result of a dispute.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי and רבא disagree about eating. Both agree the bread cannot be eaten. The question is what else differs.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two explanations given in steps 12 and 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halachic difference between אביי's and רבא's explanations of רבי.

steps.title: They differ on whether redemption money becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the bread's holiness passes onto its redemption money. According to אביי, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether the holiness passes onto its redemption money. According to אביי, it does not pass onto the redemption money. According to רבא, it does pass onto the redemption money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is about redeeming the bread with money. Does the money become holy in its place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the bread is fully holy, so when it is redeemed, the holiness moves onto the money. אביי holds that the holiness is incomplete, so it is not strong enough to pass onto the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption. Money is given in place of a holy item.
To take hold of. Here it means holiness passing onto something else.
It takes hold. The holiness passes onto the money.
There is.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the holiness is incomplete, so the money stays ordinary. רבא says the holiness is complete, so the money becomes holy.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding whether its redemption money takes on the holiness:
phrases.notes: Literally 'to grab its redemption.' The question is whether the money used to redeem the bread becomes holy in its place.

phrases.english: According to אביי, it does not pass holiness onto its redemption money,
According to רבא, it does pass holiness onto its redemption money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether the holiness transfers to the redemption money: according to רבא it does, according to אביי it does not.

steps.title: According to אביי, how is רבי different from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: For רבא, רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון clearly differ. But according to אביי, where is the difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to רבא; that is the difference between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. But according to אביי, what difference is there between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's explanation. If רבי's 'holy' bread has only weak holiness, how is his view any different from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the bread is not holy at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the difference is clear: רבי says fully holy, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says not holy. But for אביי, the bread cannot be eaten and its holiness does not even pass onto money. That looks almost the same as having no holiness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well. This opens 'it is fine for this view, but there is a problem for the other.'
But. This introduces the side that has the problem.
That is. This shows how something is explained.

phrases.english: It works well according to רבא,
that is the difference between רבי
and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
But according to אביי,
what difference is there between רבי
and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15. Because אביי's weak holiness does not even pass onto money, it seems to erase the dispute between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation of רבי's 'holy and not holy.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bread cannot be eaten and its holiness does not pass onto money, אביי's version of רבי seems the same as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the bread is not holy at all.

steps.title: They differ on whether the bread becomes unfit by leaving the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Even for אביי there is a difference: according to רבי, the bread becomes unfit if it leaves the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding becoming unfit by leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends אביי. Even weak holiness has a real result: the bread becomes unfit if it goes out of the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the bread has some holiness, so leaving the courtyard makes it unfit. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the bread is not holy at all, so leaving does nothing to it.

keyTerms.meaning: To become unfit.
Something holy that left its permitted area. That makes it unfit.
The Temple courtyard, where this bread has to stay.

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי's weak holiness still counts for something: the bread becomes unfit if it leaves the courtyard.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: regarding becoming unfit by leaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different practical result of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to אביי, רבי's weak holiness has no practical effect, so his view would be the same as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weak holiness still makes the bread unfit if it leaves the courtyard, while bread with no holiness is unaffected.

steps.title: May the bread be eaten if the lambs' blood was sprinkled for the wrong purpose?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק asks רבי חייא בר אבא whether the bread may be eaten when the עצרת lambs were slaughtered לשמן but their blood was sprinkled שלא לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק asked רבי חייא בר אבא: The lambs of עצרת that one slaughtered for their own purpose, but whose blood he sprinkled not for their own purpose: what is the law about eating that bread?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is about the same 'mixed' case: what is the law about eating the bread?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughtering was done correctly, but the sprinkling was done for the wrong purpose. The question is whether this is enough to let the bread be eaten. The next steps (19-22) first work out whose view this question follows.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him. This introduces a real, open question put to a teacher.
What is the law? This introduces an open question.
Regarding eating.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
phrases.english: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק asked
of רבי חייא בר אבא:
The lambs of עצרת that one slaughtered for their own purpose,
phrases.notes: עצרת is שבועות. These lambs are brought together with the two loaves.

phrases.english: but he sprinkled their blood not for their own purpose,
what is the law about eating that bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the same mixed case discussed by רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the bread may be eaten when the lambs were slaughtered לשמן but their blood was sprinkled שלא לשמן.

steps.title: According to whom was the question asked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question from Step 18. Under רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and under רבי, the answer is already obvious, so there seems to be nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this question based on? If it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, he says the sprinkling is what makes the bread holy. If it follows רבי, then both אביי and רבא agree the bread is holy but not permitted to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking whether the question asked in Step 18 even makes sense. Under both known opinions, the answer seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, only זריקה makes the bread holy, so a bad sprinkling cannot make it holy or permit it. For רבי, שחיטה already made the bread holy, and both אביי and רבא agree it stays holy but is not permitted. Either way there is no real doubt, so the question needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?
Sprinkling the blood of the offering on the מזבח
Makes holy (consecrates)
Holy, but not permitted to be eaten

phrases.english: According to whom?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן –
phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
doesn't he say that it is the sprinkling that makes it holy!
If according to Rebbi,
whether according to Abaye or according to Rava,
it is holy but not permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in Step 18 is a real question under any known opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק (Step 18)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under both known views the answer is already clear, so the question seems pointless.

steps.title: The question follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question follows the תנא of a ברייתא taught by the father of רבי ירמיה בר אבא. In that ברייתא, רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue whether loaves that left the courtyard can become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question follows this תנא, as the father of רבי ירמיה בר אבא taught: if the two loaves left the courtyard between the שחיטה and the זריקה, and then the כהן sprinkled the lambs' blood with the intention of eating them past their time, רבי אליעזר says the bread does not become פיגול, and רבי עקיבא says the bread does become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming a different תנא whose view makes the question a real one. It then quotes his ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the sprinkling still has an effect on the loaves even after the שחיטה, at least according to רבי עקיבא, who says it can make them פיגול. Since sprinkling still matters for the bread here, it makes sense to ask whether a sprinkling שלא לשמן permits the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות together with the lambs
An offering made forbidden by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Beyond their allowed time for eating
That went out (of the courtyard)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about loaves that were brought back. The loaves left the courtyard and stayed out, and the argument is whether the sprinkling inside can still affect them.

phrases.english: Rather, according to this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: as the father of Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba teaches:
The two loaves that went out
between the slaughtering and the sprinkling,

phrases.aramaic: וְזָרַק דָּמָן שֶׁל כְּבָשִׂים חוּץ לִזְמַנָּן –
phrases.english: and he sprinkled the blood of the lambs beyond their time –
phrases.notes: He means the כהן sprinkled while intending that the meat be eaten after its allowed time.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין בַּלֶּחֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: the bread is not subject to piggul;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ בַּלֶּחֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: the bread is subject to piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by placing the question within a third תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the question to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question could only follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון or רבי, so it would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows the תנא of the ברייתא of רבי ירמיה בר אבא's father, where sprinkling still affects the loaves.

steps.title: Both תנאים agree with רבי that שחיטה makes the loaves holy
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that both רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא hold like רבי, that the שחיטה makes the bread holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: these תנאים both hold like רבי, who says that שחיטה makes the bread holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins explaining the ברייתא. He first tells us what both sides agree on, which sets up the explanation of their argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שחיטה already made the loaves holy, leaving the courtyard matters for them. This shared starting point means the argument is not about when the bread becomes holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Sages of the משנה period (here, רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא)
They hold, they are of the opinion
The slaughtering makes the bread holy

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: these tanna'im
hold like Rebbi,
who said: the slaughtering makes it holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כְּרַבִּי סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the shared starting point of the two תנאים in the ברייתא of Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא agree with רבי that שחיטה makes the loaves holy.

steps.title: The real argument: does זריקה work on something that left the courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that each תנא follows his own known view. רבי אליעזר holds that זריקה does not affect something that left the courtyard, and רבי עקיבא holds that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, since he says sprinkling does not work for something that went out. רבי עקיבא follows his own reasoning, since he says sprinkling does work for something that went out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his explanation by showing where the two תנאים actually disagree. They argue about whether a sprinkling inside the courtyard can affect items that are outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the loaves left before the זריקה, so the sprinkling does not reach them and they cannot become פיגול. For רבי עקיבא, the זריקה still works on them, so the bad intention makes them פיגול. Each view matches a position the תנא holds elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: However, but
Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere
Is effective, has an effect
Something holy that went out of the courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: All agree that שחיטה makes the loaves holy. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue only about whether זריקה affects loaves that are outside the courtyard. This is the view that makes the Step 18 question a real one.

phrases.english: However, Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning,
for he says sprinkling is not effective for what went out,
and Rabbi Akiva follows his own reasoning,
for he says sprinkling is effective for what went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's explanation from Step 21 by identifying the point of disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר holds that זריקה does not affect what left the courtyard. רבי עקיבא holds that it does.
